category_title: Low-achieving students who read extensively but lack interactive build-on contributions due to lack of confidence
student_description: This student is highly engaged in reading but avoids building on peers' digital notes due to a deep-seated fear that their ideas are inadequate. They tend to fixate on surface-level quantitative analytics and require structured metacognitive scaffolding, as well as physical collaborative preparation, to build the self-efficacy needed for digital knowledge building.

criteria.rationale: Since the student avoids digital interaction out of anxiety, building communication skills through tangible, low-stakes physical collaboration builds the self-efficacy needed for online participation.
criteria.check: The long-term plan includes physical, offline collaborative activities (e.g., tangible mind-maps or knowledge walls) to build communication skills prior to or alongside digital platform engagement.

criteria.rationale: The student fears their initial ideas aren't 'good enough,' so establishing a culture where ideas are expected to be improved collectively reduces the pressure of perfection.
criteria.check: The long-term plan explicitly incorporates teaching norms around 'idea improvement' and collective responsibility, framing student contributions as starting points rather than final products.

criteria.rationale: Regular verbal discourse helps the student practice higher-order thinking and peer interaction in a supportive, dynamic environment before committing ideas to the digital forum.
criteria.check: The long-term plan integrates frequent, structured classroom discussions or productive verbal discourse to deepen inquiry and build confidence before digital posting.
